subject: Biology
description: Lungs, gas exchange, cellular respiration, key terms

questions.stem: The primary site of gas exchange in the human lungs is:
questions.explanation: Alveoli — tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries. Massive surface area (~70 sq m) for O₂-CO₂ exchange. ~300 million per lung. Bronchi and trachea are conducting airways; larynx is the voice box.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration: Glycolysis (2 ATP) + Krebs cycle (2 ATP) + electron transport chain (~26-28 ATP) = ~30-32 ATP/glucose. Anaerobic (fermentation): only 2 ATP (in humans, lactic-acid fermentation).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The muscular partition between the thoracic and abdominal cavities — critical for breathing — is the:
questions.explanation: Diaphragm — dome-shaped skeletal muscle. Contracts and flattens during inhalation, increasing chest-cavity volume. Pleura — membrane around lungs; Pericardium — around heart. Intercostal muscles also aid breathing.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Oxygen is transported in blood MAINLY by:
questions.explanation: ~98% of oxygen in blood is carried by haemoglobin in RBCs. ~2% dissolved in plasma. Haemoglobin is an iron-containing protein; each molecule carries up to 4 O₂. CO₂ is transported ~70% as bicarbonate, ~20% as carbamino-haemoglobin, ~10% dissolved.

options.option_text: Maximum volume of air the lungs can hold
Volume of air inhaled OR exhaled in one NORMAL breath (~500 mL)
Air remaining in lungs after a maximal exhalation
Air that can never be exhaled

questions.explanation: Tidal volume (TV) ~500 mL/breath for a normal adult. Other key volumes: Inspiratory Reserve Volume (~3000 mL), Expiratory Reserve Volume (~1100 mL), Residual Volume (~1200 mL, can never exhaled). Total lung capacity ~6 L.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The disease caused by bacteria (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) affecting the LUNGS mainly is:
questions.explanation: TB — bacterial (M. tuberculosis). Affects primarily lungs (pulmonary TB) but can affect other organs (extrapulmonary TB). Diagnosed by sputum smear + GeneXpert / X-ray. Treatment: DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment Short-course) — 6-month antibiotic combo.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.explanation: Yeast (alcoholic fermentation): glucose → ethanol + CO₂ + 2 ATP. Used in bread-making (CO₂ leavens), brewing, winemaking. Human muscles (anaerobic): glucose → lactic acid (causes cramps during intense exercise).
